name: Gareth Parker
life: “I still remember my son's first good conversation on a boat with no wind.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Gareth by a small Friday habit. Gareth prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I don't want the boat. I want the one time a week my son talks to me without looking down.
appearance: Gareth is easy to recognize by a dark undercut with a longer wave on top and one cheek that creases before the other. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a narrow brass watch set a little fast, Gareth gives a little nod before asking a hard question when listening.
personality: Gareth often says yes too quickly out of pride in being useful. The people closest to Gareth have learned to ask again the next morning, when the answer is more likely to account for sleep.
agenda: To keep a weekly conversation with the son afloat.
family: Jamie Jiang is Gareth’s older cousin. Gareth asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Jamie chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The widow's razor*, Jamie says, “I was the last customer she shaved. I asked the widow why there was still a little soap in the hinge.”
connections: Pablo Roy (former spouse). Former spouses decide whether a Sunday afloat and an hour repairing ashore have equal weight.

reactions.situation: A child wants both separated adults on the same boat
reactions.response: Gareth asks each adult whether sharing one trip is possible without putting the child in the middle.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Gareth sits beside them without expecting a performance and asks if they want to go outside.

reactions.situation: When two people ask for the same hour
reactions.response: Gareth rings both of them before quietly counting on somebody else to fill in.
